source.paraphrase: Triple-slash reference directives are a legacy way to pull in declarations. Modules state their dependencies with imports.

invariants.why: A reference directive hides the dependency from the module graph. Imports name the dependency where the file declares it.
invariants.fixHint: Replace the directive with an import of the types the file uses.
invariants.avoid: A types directive is the same mechanism as a path directive. Both must become imports.

source.paraphrase: A global augmentation adds bindings to every module at once. Prefer explicit imports that name what a module needs.

invariants.why: A declare global block lets any file depend on bindings no import names, so removing the augmentation breaks distant files silently.
invariants.fixHint: Move the declarations to a module and import them where they are used.
invariants.avoid: declare module is a different shape and stays allowed. A single var inside declare global is still a global augmentation.

source.paraphrase: A default export should carry a name. An anonymous default leaves stack traces and tooling with nothing to display.

invariants.why: An anonymous default export shows up as unknown in stack traces and breaks fast refresh, which keys on the component name.
invariants.fixHint: Name the function before default-exporting it, or export a named binding.
invariants.avoid: Adding async does not name the function. Only a binding with a name counts.

source.paraphrase: export = is the legacy CommonJS interop form. Modules publish their surface with named exports.

invariants.why: An export assignment replaces the whole module surface with one value, so adding a second export changes what every importer receives.
invariants.fixHint: Export each binding by name, and default-export a named binding where an entry point needs one.
invariants.avoid: Assigning an object literal is the same form as assigning an identifier. export default is a different syntax and stays allowed.

relations.why: A public constructor parameter property is reported by TS-LEGACY-005 as a parameter property and by DDD-ENT-002 as mutable domain state.
relations.settle: Declare a private field and assign it in the constructor body; that satisfies both rules.

relations.why: NEST-CTRL-001 tells controllers to receive providers as private readonly constructor parameters, and TS-LEGACY-005 denies constructor parameter properties.
relations.settle: Nest also injects plain constructor parameters: declare the field and assign it in the constructor body to satisfy both, or exclude Nest controllers and providers from TS-LEGACY-005.

relations.why: NEST-INJ-001 tells callers to receive providers as constructor parameters, the Nest idiom being private readonly parameter properties, which TS-LEGACY-005 denies.
relations.settle: Nest also injects plain constructor parameters: declare the field and assign it in the constructor body to satisfy both, or exclude Nest controllers and providers from TS-LEGACY-005.

source.paraphrase: A visibility modifier on a constructor parameter silently declares and assigns a field. Declare the field and assign it in the body.

invariants.why: A parameter property hides an assignment inside the signature, so a reader of the body misses state the constructor sets.
invariants.fixHint: Declare the field on the class and assign the parameter to it in the constructor body.
invariants.avoid: A mixed list with one plain parameter still declares a property for each decorated one. readonly alone on a parameter is the same declaration.

source.work: Announcing TypeScript 7.0, and the TypeScript 6.0 implementation of the import-assertion deprecation
source.paraphrase: TypeScript 7 rejects an import assertion. Write with { type: "json" } instead of assert { type: "json" }. The announcement spells the keyword asserts; the compiler diagnostic says assert.

invariants.why: TypeScript 7.0 turns the TypeScript 6.0 deprecation of import assertions into a parse error, so the file does not compile. The replacement with is valid import-attribute syntax. The rule runs only when the project installs or declares TypeScript 7.0.0 or newer, because older compilers still accept assert.
invariants.fixHint: Replace assert with with. A static import becomes import rates from "./rates.json" with { type: "json" }. A dynamic import renames the option: import("./rates.json", { with: { type: "json" } }).
invariants.avoid: with { type: "json" } is the replacement and is allowed. A return type of asserts value is T, and a call to a function named assert, are not import assertions. The announcement's spelling asserts is not the keyword the compiler rejects. A re-export such as export { row } from "./rows.json" assert { type: "json" } is not recognized by the parser this check uses. The rule stays quiet when TypeScript is missing, older than 7.0.0, or only a pre-release.
